description: Golden corpus for endpoint-auth-profile.v1 (CHAOS-4931). Read by the Go runner, the Python runner and the ajv check; never duplicate this inventory into a runner.

accept.why: TRD section 10's own example: one JWT class, exact issuer/audience/type/algorithm, current-state required, no cache, impersonation denied.
An opaque domain credential has no issuer, audience or algorithm, so `token` is omitted. Positive control that `token` is genuinely optional.
Two classes accepted, so the selector is declared. The positive half of the multi-class rule: without it the reject fixture would pass for the wrong reason.
A public route: no classes, a stated rationale, and none of the protected-route fields.
Step-up assurance and the existence-hiding disclosure mode in one profile.
Entitlement input present and impersonation deliberately allowed.
A custom-method route (/v1/authorize:batch). Boundary of the route character class.
The legacy HS256 compatibility profile (TRD section 16) is expressible, so the enum is not accidentally EdDSA-only.
Two signed classes with different algorithms: `tokens` states each class's pins, keyed by class id (CHAOS-10173). The positive half of the exactly-one-of rule.

reject.why: A route accepting a signed-token class with no issuer/audience/type/algorithm would accept any token of that class. Only the token then-branch rejects this.
The same rule for a second class, so it is not specific to one name.
An opaque credential with signed-token pins: the pins describe a token that does not exist, and a verifier built from them would look for one. The forbid direction of the token rule.
auth_js_browser_session is an encrypted JWT the algorithm enum cannot name; refused instead of accepted without pins.
A second signed class in the pinned list: the rule is a class list, not one name.
An unknown credential class is a validation error, not an extension point (CHAOS-3271 class).
Two classes and no selector: the undeclared multi-class path TRD section 10 says CI must fail. Only the then-branch of the multi-class rule rejects this.
A protected route with no action. Only the protected else-branch rejects this.
A bare action (`admin`) is the is_admin-style check ACP-ADR-05 forbids; same syntax rule as principal.v1.
alg=none is unrepresentable.
The algorithm set is closed; an algorithm nobody decided on does not slip in.
A field inviting validator fan-out is not in the contract; additionalProperties false is what makes that absence enforceable.
There is no 'try each' selector kind. Validator fan-out is the defect the profile exists to remove.
A selector kind with no name selects nothing.
A protected route that accepts no class is unauthenticatable or silently open.
A public route that lists classes contradicts itself.
A public route must say why.
current_state_required true with a cache class other than none: a stale allow on a route that declared it needs current state.
Caller-supplied resolution is not a resolver: closed set.
Closed tenant requirement set.
Closed cache class set (TRD section 14).
Closed: denied or allowed.
Closed: forbidden or not_found. A route cannot invent its own disclosure.
Assurance comes from principal.v1's closed set by reference.
A repeated class would make set-equality and the multi-class rule disagree about how many classes there are. A selector is declared so only uniqueItems fires.
A relying party rejects an unrecognised version.
A route is a path, not a URL: no query, host or whitespace.
ASCII path characters only. Pins the explicit class against a Unicode-aware shorthand.
Methods are upper case and closed.
Classification is referenced from the inventory schema; an unknown value fails through the reference, proving the reference is live.
A protected route must state current_state_required; a missing boolean cannot be read as false.
A protected route must choose how a denial is disclosed.
The string "true" is not a boolean.
Issuer, audience, type and algorithm are all or none.
An empty expected audience disables audience checking in widely used JWT libraries (G-13); the referenced principal.v1 definition forbids it.
Entitlement keys are lowercase tokens.
`token` and `tokens` together: exactly one carries the pins.
Two pinned classes with one `token` cannot state both algorithms; `tokens` is required.
`tokens` is for two or more pinned classes; one pinned class still needs its `token`.
Every pinned class the route accepts needs its own pins in `tokens`.
A pinned class the route does not accept must not appear in `tokens`.
`tokens` is keyed by the pinned class ids only.
